title: 12 Haunted Attractions to Visit in Maine For 2026
excerpt: From haunted trails to frightening haunted houses, here are 12 different Halloween-themed attractions throughout the state for 2026
content:
It's just about that time again in Maine. The leaves begin changing color on the trees, there is a crispness in the air and all things Halloween begin to pop up across the state.

For some, fall activities don't include anything scary. It's all about corn mazes, pumpkin patches and some delicious apple cider donuts.

There Are Many Real Haunted Places in Maine You Can Visit

Before we dig in on the places that operate with the intention of scaring you, Maine is actually home to a lot of places that don't intend to scare you but might.

Given its rich history, Maine is home to plentiful houses, rivers, graveyards and more that many believe carry curses, ghosts or are just generally haunted.

Be advised that many of these places often carry visitation restrictions or sit on private property.

You Can Spend an Entire Month Visiting Haunted Attractions Across Maine

In case you haven't noticed, Maine people have been embracing Halloween more and more in recent years. From Spirit Halloween expanding their footprint to people creating their own Halloween scenes in front yards.

For 2026, Maine did lose one of its premiere haunted attractions. The Farmington Fright Fest decided to cease operations. The Farmington Fright Fest thanked the countless visitors, cast and crew that made the attraction a huge hit over the years.

There are still plenty of haunted attractions to discover in Maine for 2026. Here's a list of a dozen that range from family-friendly to light scares to downright bone-chilling.
